title: SELF-DEFENCE
mv: Let the high praises of God be in their mouth, And a two-edged sword in their hand.
mvp: “Let the high praises of God be in their mouth, And a two-edged sword in their hand.” Psalm 149:6 (NKJV)
assignment: Mention five (5) Bible characters who were attacked physically and how they responded to the attack. Give a scriptural reference for each (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: As Christians, we believe that God protects us from both physical and spiritual attacks (Psalm 7:10; Zechariah 12:8) because He remains our strength and safety (Psalm 28:7). However, in the world today, crime and violence are on the increase and often arise without warning. Christians are like sheep among wolves (Matthew 10:16); often in a vulnerable state, trying to maintain peace and protect themselves, whereas the scriptures admonish us to act with wisdom and preparedness (Proverbs 22:3). Today’s lesson explores the biblical balance between self-protection and righteousness in moments of threat.

Self-defence here is defined as "protecting oneself from injury at the hand of others." Self-defence involves preserving one's health, life and property when it is threatened by the actions of others (Nehemiah 4:7-23; Luke 11:21).

There is a distinction between self-defence and vengeance, retaliation or reprisal attack. Self-defence is neither about taking vengeance nor about premeditated attack on others. Some situations may call for self-defence, but not retaliation in kind (Matthew 5:38-42). Our self-defence is not a vengeful reaction to an offence. In fact, many offences can simply be absorbed in forbearance and love (Romans 12:17-21).

The Bible gives some clues about God’s attitude toward self-defence: “If a thief is caught breaking in at night and is struck a fatal blow, the defender is not guilty of bloodshed; but if it happens after sunrise, the defender is guilty of bloodshed” (Exodus 22:2-3 NIV). Two basic principles taught in this text are the right to own private property and the right to defend that property.

Also, Jesus explicitly commands His followers to buy a sword, even if they have to sell their cloak to do so (Luke 22:35-38). Jesus knew that there would be a time when His followers would be threatened, and He upheld their right to self-defence. Jesus took prudent measures to protect Himself from harm until it was time for Him to die (Matthew 17:22-23).

The Bible never forbids self-defence (Psalm 144:1), and believers are allowed to defend themselves and their families (1 Samuel 30:1-8; Acts 7:24). The proper use of self-defence has to do with wisdom, understanding and tact. We must have ‘wisdom that comes from heaven’ regarding when to fight and when not to, so as not to make a dangerous situation worse (James 1:5; 3:17).

The full exercise of the right to self-defence depends on the situation. No one should be too quick to use deadly force against another, except in a situation of ‘kill or be killed’. Homes, Organizations, Schools, and especially Churches should intentionally make adequate preparation by all means necessary to always protect the lives and properties of those they are responsible for. They should invest more in technological monitoring devices such as CCTVs, etc. A trained intelligence team should also be set up to observe and alert against any threat lurking around. Also, defence mechanisms should be put in place to combat any threat to lives and properties. Usual activities, Church services and programmes should also be restructured by leaders of various groups, just like it was done during the COVID-19 Pandemic to minimise avoidable exposures to attacks.
It is expedient for every Christian, Church or Organisation to learn survival/self-defence skills.
The prevailing security situation makes it necessary for every believer to learn how to defend themselves within the confines of the law.

i: Briefly explain the biblical stance on self-defence.
What should Christians do to defend themselves?
